what_it_supplies: Twenty-three 50×30-foot cribs placed during 1870, 18–26 feet deep, making 1,150 feet up to water surface.
Six additional 50×30-foot cribs in spring 1871; total 29 cribs and 1,450 feet, including a 300-foot westward return at the north end.
May 30, 1871 contract with Illinois Central Railroad Company for continuation.
Reported and projected superstructure and extension quantities, with distinct dating limits.
what_it_does_not_supply: A registered footprint or absolute coordinates for the 1870–1871 outer breakwater.
A reconciled 8 October 1871 superstructure extent: summary reports about 200 feet, while Appendix A16 reports 1,000 feet at writing.
Proof that the projected 900-foot extension or roughly 2,000-foot completed structure existed by the fire.
note: Post-fire publication: use explicitly dated 1870 and spring 1871 construction statements. Houston’s Appendix A covers the fiscal year ending June 30, 1871, but at writing has no separate date on A16. The 200/1,000-foot superstructure reporting difference remains unresolved. Evidence ledger: data/traces/harbor_1869/construction_ledger_1870_1871.json. This source supersedes relying solely on the earlier 800-foot contract as evidence of built work.
